```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(pdmS7)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  error = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 3.8, dpi = 120
)
logger::log_threshold(logger::WARN, namespace = "pdmS7")
pal <- c("#236b83", "#a26421", "#5b8c3a", "#8a3b6b", "#444444", "#b23b3b", "#9aa7b0")
```

Manual calibration is judgement: a hydrologist reads a hydrograph, changes a parameter, and
decides whether the model is better. A calibration can be defended later only if that
judgement was recorded as it happened and cannot be quietly rewritten. The calibration log
does this. Every action writes one entry to a project folder: who, when, which data and
parameters, the scores, and the reasoning. Entries are never edited, each carries a
checksum of the one before, and a report is generated from them.

This article walks through one calibration, from project start to sign-off. The
[design record](../calibration-log-design.html) explains the decisions behind it. The same
steps are available without code in the app, `calibration_app()`.

# Who is writing

Every entry records a declared name and role, with the operating-system login. Roles follow
the governance framework: a **Custodian** does the calibration; a **Steward** (or Delegated
Steward) signs it off; the **Owner** is named as accountable.

```{r identity}
options(pdmS7.user = "Ann Hydrologist", pdmS7.role = "custodian")
```

Set these once per session, or in `.Renviron` as `PDMS7_USER` and `PDMS7_ROLE`.

# Starting the project

```{r start}
project <- file.path(tempdir(), "brook-calibration")
start_calibration_project(
  project, catchment = "Example Brook", gauge = "99001", purpose = "Flood forecasting",
  area_km2 = 40, owner = "Deputy Director", steward = "Sam Steward"
)
```

The data here are synthetic: four months of hourly rainfall, and the flow of a "true"
catchment with gauging noise and a three-day gap.

```{r data}
set.seed(42)
n <- 24 * 120
time <- seq(as.POSIXct("2023-10-01", tz = "UTC"), by = 3600, length.out = n)
forcing <- data.frame(
  time = time, rain = ifelse(stats::runif(n) < 0.07, stats::rgamma(n, 0.7, scale = 3), 0),
  pet = 0.06
)
truth <- pdm_presets("standard")
truth$area_km2 <- 40
truth$fc <- 1.15
truth$recharge$kg <- 60
truth$surface$k1 <- 3
truth$surface$k2 <- 8
observed <- run_pdm(pdm_from_config(truth), forcing)$output$q_m3s *
  exp(stats::rnorm(n, 0, 0.04))
observed[1500:1572] <- NA
```

# Registering the data

Registration copies the data into the project, takes their checksums, records their
quality, and fixes the scorecard: the calibration and validation windows, the headline
score and the starting soil moisture. Every later run is scored the same way, so trials can
be compared fairly. Rows before the calibration window are warm-up.

```{r register}
reg <- register_data(
  project, forcing, observed,
  calibration = c("2023-10-15", "2023-12-31"),
  validation = c("2024-01-01", "2024-01-28"),
  headline = "nse", reasoning = "Gauge record checked against the station log."
)
str(reg$summary[c("rows", "start", "end", "observed_missing", "observed_longest_gap")])
```

# Choosing the structure

```{r structure}
start <- pdm_presets("standard")
start$area_km2 <- 40
select_structure(project, start,
                 reasoning = "Standard PDM as the starting point for a responsive clay catchment.")
```

The structure is run and scored like any trial, so it is the root of the calibration path.

# Trials

`preview_trial()` runs a change without logging it, so you can look before you commit.

```{r preview, fig.cap="The preview against its parent over part of the calibration window."}
preview <- preview_trial(project, parent = 3, changes = c(fc = 1.15))
rows <- preview$rows[1:(24 * 30)]
parent <- run_pdm(pdm_from_config(start), forcing)$output$q_m3s
top <- max(observed[rows], parent[rows], preview$simulated[rows], na.rm = TRUE) * 1.25
par(mar = c(3, 4.2, 0.6, 0.6))
plot(time[rows], observed[rows], pch = 16, cex = 0.3, col = pal[5], xlab = "",
     ylab = "Flow (m3/s)", ylim = c(0, top))
lines(time[rows], parent[rows], col = pal[7], lwd = 1.5)
lines(time[rows], preview$simulated[rows], col = pal[1], lwd = 1.5)
legend("topleft", c("observed", "parent (0003)", "preview"), bty = "n", horiz = TRUE,
       col = c(pal[5], pal[7], pal[1]), pch = c(16, NA, NA), lty = c(NA, 1, 1))
round(rbind(parent = unlist(project_trials(project)[1, c("nse", "volume_error", "kge_alpha")]),
            preview = unlist(preview$scores[c("nse", "volume_error", "kge_alpha")])), 3)
```

The volume error has gone from 12 per cent too dry to near zero, but the NSE has fallen
slightly: the variability ratio shows the peaks are now too large. The trial is still an
improvement, because the water balance is right and the peaks are a separate question.
That judgement is the hydrologist's, not the headline score's, and the log records it with
its reason:

```{r trials}
log_trial(project, parent = 3, changes = c(fc = 1.15), verdict = "better",
          reasoning = "Volume 12 per cent low; raised the rainfall factor. Peaks now too big.")
log_trial(project, parent = 4, changes = c(recharge.kg = 10), verdict = "worse",
          reasoning = "Faster recharge to move peak water into baseflow; recessions far too high.")
log_trial(project, parent = 4, changes = c(recharge.kg = 60), verdict = "better",
          reasoning = "Slower recharge instead; peaks and recessions both match.")
log_trial(project, parent = 6, changes = c(surface.k1 = 3, surface.k2 = 8),
          verdict = "better", reasoning = "Peaks slightly early; slowed the surface cascade.")
```

Trial 0005 was a dead end; trial 0006 went back to 0004 and tried the other way. The log
keeps both, because a defensible calibration includes what was tried and rejected.

A short automatic calibration can polish the result. It is logged like a trial, with its
bounds, seed and the table of every start.

```{r auto}
auto <- log_auto_calibration(
  project, parent = 7, lower = c(surface.k1 = 1, surface.k2 = 3),
  upper = c(surface.k1 = 6, surface.k2 = 15), starts = 3, seed = 1,
  control = list(maxit = 30), reasoning = "Fine-tune the routing within physical bounds."
)
log_note(project, "The January gap is a logger fault, not low flow.", refers_to = 2)
```

# The calibration path

```{r path, fig.cap="Every run by its NSE on the calibration window. Lines join each run to its parent; colour shows the verdict."}
trials <- project_trials(project)
trials[, .(id, type, parent, changes, verdict, nse = round(nse, 3),
           volume_error = round(volume_error, 3))]
x <- seq_len(nrow(trials))
colour <- ifelse(trials$type == "auto_calibration", pal[1],
                 ifelse(is.na(trials$verdict), pal[5],
                        ifelse(trials$verdict == "better", pal[3], pal[6])))
plot(x, trials$nse, pch = 16, col = colour, cex = 1.6, xaxt = "n", xlab = "",
     ylab = "NSE, calibration window")
axis(1, at = x, labels = trials$id)
parents <- match(trials$parent, trials$id)
segments(x[parents], trials$nse[parents], x, trials$nse, col = pal[7])
```

# Candidate and validation

The candidate is rerun before it is accepted, and must reproduce its recorded output
exactly. Validation scores the validation window, once.

```{r candidate}
propose_candidate(project, entry = auto$id,
                  reasoning = "Best NSE with physically sensible time constants.")
val <- validate_candidate(project, reasoning = "Holds up on January.")
round(data.frame(calibration = unlist(val$calibration_scores),
                 validation = unlist(val$validation_scores))[c("nse", "kge", "volume_error",
                                                               "fdc_high"), ], 3)
```

# Sign-off

Only a Steward or Delegated Steward can sign off, and not one who wrote any of the
calibration. The package checks both the declared name and the login, so a Steward cannot
sign off from the Custodian's session:

```{r self}
options(pdmS7.user = "Sam Steward", pdmS7.role = "steward")
reviewed <- c(integrity = TRUE, data = TRUE, calibration_path = TRUE, validation = TRUE)
tryCatch(sign_off_project(project, "Accepted.", reviewed),
         error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))
```

In practice the Steward signs off on their own machine, or in the app. Below we stand in
for that machine by giving the Steward a different login.

```{r steward-login, include=FALSE}
real_login <- pdmS7:::.login
utils::assignInNamespace(".login", function() "sam.steward", "pdmS7")
```

```{r signoff}
sign_off_project(project, "Reviewed the path, data and validation. Accepted for forecasting.",
                 reviewed)
read_project(project)$status
```

```{r restore-login, include=FALSE}
utils::assignInNamespace(".login", real_login, "pdmS7")
```

A signed-off project accepts nothing further until a Steward reopens it with a reason.

# Integrity

`verify_project()` recomputes every checksum and, with `rerun = TRUE`, repeats every run.

```{r verify}
checks <- verify_project(project, rerun = TRUE)
checks[, .N, by = .(check, ok)]
```

Now suppose someone tidies the reasoning of trial 0005 after the event:

```{r tamper}
file <- file.path(project, "entries", "0005-trial.yml")
original <- readLines(file)
writeLines(sub("recessions far too high", "recessions slightly high", original), file)
verify_project(project)[ok == FALSE]
writeLines(original, file)
```

The edit is caught at the next entry, whose stored checksum no longer matches. Changed data
files and runs that no longer reproduce are caught the same way.

# The report

```{r report, eval=FALSE}
build_report(project)
```

`build_report()` writes `report/report.html`, a single file with embedded figures that can
be attached to a review, and a Markdown copy. It opens with the integrity result, then
shows the data, the structure, the calibration path, the candidate's hydrographs and
flow-duration curves for both windows, parameter sensitivity, the sign-off and the final
configuration with every entry's checksum.

# Tracing operational runs

Once a calibration is in use, the question changes from "how was it calibrated" to "which
calibration produced this forecast". The run log answers it. It is off by default.

```{r runlog}
register <- file.path(dirname(project), "approved.yml")
writeLines(c("projects:", paste0("  - ", basename(project))), register)
options(pdmS7.run_log = file.path(tempdir(), "runs.csv"), pdmS7.register = register,
        pdmS7.run_tag = "forecast 2024-02-01 06:00")
approved <- pdm_from_config(auto$configuration)
recent <- forcing[2700:2880, ]
forecast <- run_pdm(approved, recent)
check <- run_pdm(pdm_from_config(start), recent)
read_run_log()[, .(tag, fingerprint = substr(fingerprint, 1, 8), rows, status, approval,
                   project, sign_off)]
```

The first run used the signed-off parameters and is marked `approved`, with the project and
sign-off entry; the second used the uncalibrated structure and is marked `unapproved`.
Neither was blocked. If the project is reopened, runs with the old parameters are marked
`superseded`.

```{r cleanup, include=FALSE}
options(pdmS7.run_log = NULL, pdmS7.register = NULL, pdmS7.run_tag = NULL,
        pdmS7.user = NULL, pdmS7.role = NULL)
unlink(c(project, register, file.path(tempdir(), "runs.csv")), recursive = TRUE)
```

# Summary

| Step | Function |
|---|---|
| Declare who you are | `options(pdmS7.user = , pdmS7.role = )` |
| Start | `start_calibration_project()` |
| Data and scorecard | `register_data()` |
| Structure | `select_structure()` |
| Try, then log | `preview_trial()`, `log_trial()`, `log_auto_calibration()`, `log_note()` |
| Decide | `propose_candidate()`, `validate_candidate()` |
| Approve | `sign_off_project()`, `reopen_project()` |
| Check and report | `verify_project()`, `build_report()`, `project_trials()` |
| Trace use | `options(pdmS7.run_log = , pdmS7.register = )`, `read_run_log()` |
